links.outcome: Calibration and net benefit of published CVD risk models applied to a different population
links.effect: Calibration varied substantially: PROCAM, Framingham, ASSIGN, QRISK1 overestimated risk; PREVENT, PREDICT, SCORE, SCORE2, SCORE2-OP, China-PAR generally underestimated. Ten-year AUC ranged 0.668 to 0.734.
links.quote: Direct application of cardiovascular risk scores across populations can produce clinically important differences in calibration and net benefit.

links.outcome: Whether discrimination alone reflects calibration and clinical utility of risk models
links.effect: AUC ranged 0.668 to 0.734 while calibration varied substantially and net benefit diverged at higher treatment thresholds; QRISK2 had best calibration, PREVENT lowest Brier score.
links.quote: Model selection for primary prevention should require external validation, local recalibration, and assessment of clinical utility, rather than reliance on discrimination alone.

links.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of 16 candidate risk models on the same cohort data
links.effect: Models differed markedly in calibration and net benefit; composite assessment favored PREVENT, QRISK2, PREDICT, PCE, and northern China-PAR variants.
links.quote: Composite assessment favored PREVENT, QRISK2, PREDICT, PCE, and northern China-PAR variants.

unlisted_practices: Decision curve analysis for net benefit assessment of risk models

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation and head-to-head comparison of 16 cardiovascular risk prediction models in UK Biobank data, evaluating discrimination, calibration, and net benefit without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard.
